narrative:
On November 18, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 23.3%, taking up 655 out of 2,810 scheduled cases across 50 judicial rosters. This represents a drop in overall hearing activity compared to prior recorded sessions, down from 42.8% on November 16, 44.0% on November 13, and 36.0% on November 12.

Individual bench performance showed significant variance. Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar in Hall 22 led conversion across multiple lists, notably hearing 46 of 70 cases (65.7%) in his main cause list. Justice E.S. Indiresh in Hall 18 heard 37 of 78 cases (47.4%), while Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde achieved a 70.0% hearing rate (21 of 30) in one session. Conversely, several large rosters saw minimal progression; Justice K. V. Aravind heard 1 of 144 listed cases (0.7%) on his main list, and the division bench of the Chief Justice & K.S. Hemalekha recorded zero heard cases on their 44-case roster.

Stage-wise conversion favored early-stage and procedural matters over long-form arguments. Preliminary Hearings achieved the highest standard stage conversion at 29.9% (112 of 375), followed by Orders at 28.4% (304 of 1,069) and Admissions at 24.5% (149 of 609). Final Hearings dropped precipitously to a 4.0% rate (21 of 530), a notable contraction from the 29.1% rate seen on November 16.

Subject matter distribution was led by Writ Petitions (WP) with 1,314 listings, though only 21.8% (286 cases) were heard—down from 46.3% on November 16. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) converted 22.8% of cases (107 of 469), compared to 37.3% on November 16. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) held higher clearance efficiency at 34.2% (146 of 427), alongside Regular Second Appeals (RSA) at 31.5% (34 of 108).
